newsitem.title: INDIA: India call ends steady, gilt prices firm on demand.
newsitem.headline: India call ends steady, gilt prices firm on demand.

text.p: Indian call money ended Thursday at 0.1-0.4 percent, little changed from opening quotes of 0.1-0.5, dealers said.
They said call money rates were stuck in a narrow band in a day marked by little demand for funds.
Two-day money was traded at 0.10 to 0.25 percent while most of the deals for four-day money were at 0.40 percent, dealers said.
They said the market was flush with liquidity and unless substantial funds were drained away, call money would remain at current levels.
"Liquidity in excess of 80 billion rupees will have to be mopped up before call money rates react from current levels," R. Narayan, treasury dealer at Bank of Nova Scotia said.
Government security prices were firm in active trade, dealers said.
"The securities market was fairly active with prices for medium-term and long-term stocks moving up by 40 to 50 paise," M. Srinivasan, treasury head at Centurion Bank said.
"There ought to be a reaction in the security prices for longer-dated securities after the 10-year gilt auction," he added.
The Reserve Bank of India holds an auction of 30 billion rupees of ten-year securities on April 21.
"The 14.00 percent government stock 2006 and 13.65 percent 2007 are expected to react after the auction," Srinivasan said.
"The market expects a cut-off around 13.25 percent at the auction," he said.
Trades on the National Stock Exchange were worth 3.93 billion rupees against Tuesday's 4.91 billion, dealers said.
The money market was inactive on Wednesday as banks in India's commercial centre of Bombay and some other centres were closed for a local holiday.
The money market is closed on Friday as banks are closed across the country for a Moslem festival.
